known_facts_book1: A man of straw with a painted face, stuffed and dressed in a Munchkin's old blue clothes, made to scare crows from a cornfield.
Dorothy lifts him off his pole and he walks with her, wanting the Great Oz to give him brains.
Cannot be hurt by falling or bruising, but is deathly afraid of a lighted match because he might burn.
Solves problems by thinking cleverly despite claiming to have no brains, proving wiser than he believes.
Is carried across a wide ditch and a river by the others, and is left stranded on a pole in the river until a Stork lifts him off.
Receives from the humbug Oz a head stuffed with bran mixed with pins and needles, which Oz calls 'bran-new brains'.
Is left by the departed Wizard to rule over the Emerald City in his place.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The girl who frees him from his pole; his closest friend.
known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: Fellow traveller; the two look after each other, the Woodman chopping and building where the Scarecrow plans.
known_relations_book1.Wizard: Gives him bran-and-pin brains and leaves him to rule the Emerald City.

known_facts_book1: A woodman made entirely of tin, found rusted motionless in the forest with his axe raised, freed when Dorothy oils his joints.
Was once a flesh-and-blood Munchkin wood-chopper in love with a Munchkin girl.
The girl's lazy old-woman guardian bribed the Wicked Witch of the East to enchant his axe, which cut off his limbs, head, and body one by one.
A tinsmith replaced each severed part with tin, but the new tin body had no heart, so he lost his love for the girl.
Wants the Great Oz to give him a heart so he can love again.
Weeps easily and must be careful, because his tears rust his jaw and joints.
Kills a wildcat that is chasing the Queen of the Field Mice, and beheads the pack of wolves the Wicked Witch of the West sends against the travellers.
Receives from Oz a heart of silk stuffed with sawdust, placed in his tin chest.
Is later asked by the Winkies to become their ruler, and agrees to return after Dorothy goes home.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The girl who oils him free; his devoted friend.
known_relations_book1.Cowardly Lion: Travelling companion he defends and is defended by.
known_relations_book1.Wicked Witch: Of the East, who enchanted his axe and cost him his flesh body; of the West, his captor whom the group destroys.

known_facts_book1: A great Lion who bounds out of the forest roaring but is really a coward, ashamed that he trembles whenever there is danger.
Joins the travellers to ask the Great Oz for courage.
Knocks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman about, then feels sorry for striking Toto, whom Dorothy defends.
Leaps the party across a wide ditch, carrying them one at a time on his back.
Falls asleep helplessly in the deadly field of scarlet poppies and is too heavy to be carried until the Field Mice haul him out on a truck.
Frightens the Wizard with a great roar the day the humbug is exposed.
Receives from Oz a dish of liquid that Oz calls courage, and drinks it down.
On the journey south is hailed by the animals of a forest as their King after he kills a giant spider that had been devouring them, and agrees to return and reign as King of Beasts.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The girl he cannot bring himself to harm; his friend and the one who scolds him for striking Toto.
known_relations_book1.Toto: The little dog he swats and then apologises for; they end up sleeping side by side.
known_relations_book1.Wizard: Gives him a drink he calls courage.
